notes: All tools are advertised together by the `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler; there is no per-tool feature flag in the provided code.
Read tools contact fixed Slack API endpoints, not agent-chosen hosts, so their READ `destination_args` are empty even when arguments select Slack records.

slack_add_reaction.rationale: `slack_add_reaction` writes an agent-supplied `reaction` to a Slack message selected by call-time `channel_id` and `timestamp` via `reactions.add`. This changes Slack state at an agent-chosen message destination, so it is a SINK.

slack_get_channel_history.rationale: `slack_get_channel_history` uses the Slack bot bearer token to call `conversations.history` for a call-time `channel_id` and returns the Slack JSON response. Channel history is SaaS data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. Slack channel messages are authored in a multi-writer channel, so message content in the returned history is UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_thread_replies.rationale: `slack_get_thread_replies` uses the Slack bot bearer token to call `conversations.replies` for a call-time `channel_id` and `thread_ts`, then returns the Slack JSON response. Thread replies are Slack workspace SaaS data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. Replies in a Slack thread are multi-writer message content and therefore UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_user_profile.rationale: `slack_get_user_profile` uses the Slack bot bearer token to call `users.profile.get` for a call-time `user_id`, then returns the Slack JSON response. Detailed Slack profile data is SaaS data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. Profile text/display fields can be authored by the profiled Slack user, so the returned profile content is UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_users.rationale: `slack_get_users` uses the Slack bot bearer token to call `users.list` and returns the Slack JSON response. Workspace user information is SaaS data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. User profile/display fields in a workspace user list can be authored by the users themselves in a multi-writer service, so the returned content is UNTRUSTED.

slack_list_channels.rationale: `slack_list_channels` uses the configured Slack bot bearer token in `botHeaders` and reads Slack channel data from `conversations.list` or `conversations.info`, then returns the raw/constructed Slack response to the agent. That is SaaS workspace data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. The returned channel objects can include workspace-authored channel metadata such as names/topics/purposes; because Slack channels are multi-writer workspace resources, this output is UNTRUSTED.

slack_post_message.rationale: `slack_post_message` sends agent-supplied `text` to Slack `chat.postMessage` for the agent-chosen `channel_id`. A Slack channel is an agent-chosen message destination, so this is a SINK. The Slack API host is fixed, but the recipient channel is call-time controlled.

slack_reply_to_thread.rationale: `slack_reply_to_thread` sends agent-supplied `text` to Slack `chat.postMessage` with call-time `channel_id` and `thread_ts`. This delivers data to an agent-chosen Slack conversation/thread, so it is a SINK.

value_conditions.default: Unset environment variables cause exit/no tools.
value_conditions.effect: The process prints an error and exits before serving tools. When both are set, the server lists all eight tools unconditionally.

value_conditions.default: Unset: list public channels in the configured team.
value_conditions.effect: For `slack_list_channels`, when set the code reads only those predefined IDs via `conversations.info`; when unset, it lists public channels via `conversations.list`. This changes list scope but does not remove the SECRET or UNTRUSTED labels.
